subject: paediatrics
title: Congenital Toxoplasmosis, Syphilis and Neonatal Tetanus

steps.tx: Transplacental transmission of the obligate intracellular protozoan parasite causes **congenital toxoplasmosis**. Infection occurs when a seronegative pregnant woman ingests undercooked meat containing tissue cysts or accidentally ingests sporulated oocysts shed in feline feces. The classic clinical presentation is defined by the historic Sabin triad: diffuse intracranial calcifications, chorioretinitis, and hydrocephalus.
steps.say: Congenital toxoplasmosis presents with the Sabin triad of hydrocephalus, calcifications, and chorioretinitis.

vis.alt: Clinical diagnostic triads of congenital infections including toxoplasmosis and syphilis.
vis.caption: Diagnostic triads of congenital toxoplasmosis, syphilis, and neonatal tetanus. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The distinctive ophthalmological lesion of congenital toxoplasmosis is **focal necrotizing chorioretinitis**. Tachyzoites preferentially invade the sensory retina, producing yellowish-white elevated lesions with surrounding retinal edema, predominantly involving the macula. As lesions heal, they leave deeply pigmented, punched-out atrophic macular chorioretinal scars that cause severe irreversible loss of central vision.
steps.say: Necrotizing chorioretinitis leaves punched-out pigmented macular scars that impair central vision.

left.title: Acute Active Chorioretinitis
points: Vitreous haze and severe retinal edema

right.title: Healed Quiescent Scars
points: Risk of reactivated chorioretinitis in childhood

steps.tx: Standard pharmacological management for congenital toxoplasmosis requires **triple therapy with pyrimethamine**. The synergistic combination comprises oral pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and folinic acid (leucovorin) administered for twelve continuous months. Folinic acid is essential to bypass pyrimethamine inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase, preventing severe bone marrow suppression and megaloblastic anemia.
steps.say: One year of pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, and folinic acid provides definitive therapy.

rows: Rescues host bone marrow from megaloblastosis

steps.tx: Transplacental transmission of the spirochete Treponema pallidum produces **early congenital syphilis**, presenting within the first two years of life. Cardinal manifestations include persistent syphilitic rhinitis or snuffles discharging highly infectious serosanguinous fluid, a maculopapular desquamating rash on the palms and soles, hepatosplenomegaly, and generalized lymphadenopathy.
steps.say: Early congenital syphilis presents with syphilitic snuffles, palm-sole rash, and hepatosplenomegaly.

rows: Teeming with active spirochetes on darkfield
Bullae on palms and soles with peeling
Classic cutaneous sign of active spirochetemia
Infant refuses to move limb due to bone pain
Symmetric erosion of medial upper tibial metaphysis

steps.tx: Late manifestations appearing after two years of age reflect chronic chronic gummatous inflammation, characterized by the pathognomonic **Hutchinson triad of congenital syphilis**. The classic triad comprises interstitial keratitis causing corneal clouding, eighth cranial nerve sensorineural deafness, and notched peg-shaped Hutchinson incisors. Additional bone deformities include saddle nose, mulberry molars, and saber shins.
steps.say: Late congenital syphilis exhibits the Hutchinson triad of notched incisors, deafness, and keratitis.

left.title: Hutchinson Classic Triad
points: Hutchinson teeth: notched, barrel-shaped central incisors
Interstitial keratitis with photophobia and corneal haze
Eighth nerve sensorineural deafness at puberty

right.title: Associated Skeletal Stigmata
points: Saddle nose deformity from nasal cartilage destruction
Saber shin from anterior tibial cortical thickening
Clutton joints: painless symmetrical knee hydrarthrosis

steps.tx: The absolute treatment of choice for congenital syphilis is **aqueous crystalline penicillin G**. Administered intravenously at fifty thousand units per kilogram per dose every twelve hours for the first seven days, then every eight hours for a total of ten to fourteen days, penicillin completely eradicates treponemal spirochetes. Procaine penicillin intramuscularly serves as an acceptable alternative.
steps.say: Aqueous crystalline penicillin G for ten to fourteen days completely cures congenital syphilis.

steps.tx: Contamination of the unhealed umbilical stump with Clostridium tetani spores causes **fatal neonatal tetanus**. Typically presenting on the fifth to seventh day of life in infants born to unvaccinated mothers, the infant stops breastfeeding due to masseter trismus and develops the sardonic grin of risus sardonicus, followed by agonizing generalized muscle spasms triggered by sound or touch.
steps.say: Neonatal tetanus presents with trismus, risus sardonicus, and spasms from unhygienic cord care.

left.title: Clinical Progression
points: Inability to suck and latch (day 5 to 7)
Trismus and risus sardonicus facial spasm

right.title: Essential Prevention
points: Maternal tetanus toxoid vaccination during pregnancy
Clean delivery and hygienic cord clamping
Universal elimination via public health immunization

steps.tx: Purulent conjunctival inflammation occurring within the first twenty-eight days of life is **neonatal ophthalmia neonatorum**. Neisseria gonorrhoeae produces hyperacute, copious, purulent discharge at two to five days post-delivery, with high risk of corneal perforation requiring immediate intravenous ceftriaxone. Chlamydia trachomatis appears at five to fourteen days, requiring oral erythromycin to treat concurrent chlamydial pneumonitis.
steps.say: Gonococcal conjunctivitis appears early with copious pus, while chlamydia appears later.

rows: Single dose IV ceftriaxone (25 to 50 mg/kg)
